subject: Avoid exponentiating a large matrix at every step

messages.author: 1384d5b2e3f82159
messages.subject: Avoid exponentiating a large matrix at every step
parts:
Hi, 

Right now I have 

exp( -(scalar_param1 + predictor_matrix*vector_param) / scalar_param2 )

in my model block, but the matrix of predictors is large (roughly 30,000 by 10) and I was hoping there was a way I could avoid repeatedly exponentiating it. Is there a way to do some computations in the transformed data block so that I'm only repeatedly exponentiating parameters (and not also data)? I'm having trouble figuring out how to do this correctly. 

Thanks in advance for any advice!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Avoid exponentiating a large matrix at every step
parts:
That depends on what you do with the value of the exp()
and where the arguments are declared --- you can only transform
data variables in the transformed data block.

Some of our distributions, like Poisson, directly accept log-scale
arguments so you don't need to exponentiate at all.

To help more, we'd need to see the model.

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Avoid exponentiating a large matrix at every step
parts:
Oops, sorry Bob, I meant to write that I have a similar question to the original poster's (I think). 

The context is a survival/duration model (with right-censoring) along the lines of the following :

functions {
  # transform normal(0,1) to cauchy
  real cauchy_trans(real loc, real scale, real noise) {
    return loc + scale * tan(pi() * (Phi_approx(noise) - 0.5)) ;
  }
}

data {
  int<lower=1>        nObs ;  # number of uncensored obs
  int<lower=1>        nCen ;  # number of censored obs
  int<lower=1>        nX ;    # number of predictors
  vector[nObs]        yObs ;  # data for uncensored obs 
  vector[nCen]        yCen ;  # data for censored obs
  matrix[nObs, nX]    xObs ;  # predictors for uncensored obs
  matrix[nCen, nX]    xCen ;  # predictors for censored obs 
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> alpha_scale_noise ;
  real<lower=0> beta_scale_noise ;
  real<lower=0> beta0_scale_noise ;
  vector[nX]    beta_noise ;
  real          beta0_noise ;
  real          alpha_noise ;
}
transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0>         alpha_scale ;
  real<lower=0>         beta_scale ;
  real<lower=0>         beta0_scale ;
  vector[nX]            beta ;
  real                  beta0 ;
  real                  alpha ;

  beta0_scale <- cauchy_trans(0, 2.5, beta0_scale_noise) ;
  alpha_scale <- cauchy_trans(0, 2.5, alpha_scale_noise) ;
  beta_scale  <- cauchy_trans(0, 2.5, beta_scale_noise) ;

  beta0 <- beta0_scale * beta0_noise ;
  alpha <- exp(alpha_scale * alpha_noise) ;
  beta  <- beta_scale * beta_noise ;
}
model {
  beta_scale_noise ~ normal(0,1) ; # --> beta_scale ~ half-cauchy(0,2.5)
  beta0_scale_noise ~ normal(0,1) ;
  alpha_scale_noise ~ normal(0,1) ;
  
  beta_noise ~ normal(0,1) ; # --> beta[i] ~ normal(0, beta_scale)
  beta0_noise ~ normal(0,1) ; 
  alpha_noise ~ normal(0,1) ;  
  
  # for the censored obs
  increment_log_prob(
    weibull_ccdf_log(yCen, alpha, exp(-(b0 + xCen*beta)/alpha))
  ) ;
  
  # for the uncensored obs
  yObs ~ weibull(alpha, exp(-(b0 + xObs*beta)/alpha)) ;
}

So like in the original poster's question I have exp(-(b0 + xObs*beta)/alpha) in the model block and xObs (and xCen too) are rather large matrices. Unfortunately I'm not working with the Poisson or another distribution permitting log-scale arguments. I've been trying to find a clever way of doing the exponentiation involving the xObs and xCen matrices only once in the transformed data block, but I haven't come up with anything satisfying. Do you see anything?

Thanks for the help!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Avoid exponentiating a large matrix at every step
parts: I don't see where b0 is declared. It's used here:
> weibull_ccdf_log(yCen, alpha, exp(-(b0 + xCen*beta)/alpha))
and
> yObs ~ weibull(alpha, exp(-(b0 + xObs*beta)/alpha)) ;

alpha: param real param
xCen: data matrix
beta: param vector
b0: ???

You could compute and assign
t1 = -b0/alpha and t2 = -beta/alpha and reuse them
to compute the inner terms

exp(t1 + t2 * xCen)

and

exp(t2 + t2 * xObs)

But none of the terms are purely data, so they can't be computed
in the transformed data block.
- Bob
